formulations.Polymer system Notes: PEO4LiCF3SO3 (O/Li = 4, Li:EO = 0.25, LiCF3SO3 mass fraction 0.47). WAXS shows the crystalline intermediate compound, only very faint PEO lines, and no free salt. The paper suggests the compound's stoichiometry is below 4 (proposed P(EO3LiCF3SO3)).
formulations.Arrhenius notes: Paper states Ea ≈ 0.7 eV for PEO-LiCF3SO3 electrolytes with salt mass fraction > ~0.05, for T > 60 °C (60-130 °C). All log σ vs 1/T curves show a knee at the eutectic melting temperature (~60 °C), with two Arrhenius regions.
formulations.Notes: Aldrich PEO with a stated high molecular weight of 900 K (which average is not specified). Films about 50 μm thick were cast from acetonitrile and dried under partial vacuum at 95-100 °C for at least 48 h. Water content was below 25 ppm. Conductivity was measured by ac impedance on heating from 25 to 130 °C without preheating.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, J. Electrochem. Soc. 133(2), 315-325 (1986), Phase Diagrams and Conductivity Characterization of Some PEO-LiX Electrolytes

formulations.Polymer system Notes: PEO8LiCF3SO3 (O/Li = 8). Two-phase (crystalline + amorphous) above 60 °C; from the phase diagram, at least 50 wt% of the electrolyte is amorphous above 60 °C. The crystalline intermediate compound is proposed to be P(EO3LiCF3SO3) (stoichiometry below 4). Eutectic near O/Li ≈ 100, melting at ~60 °C.
formulations.Arrhenius notes: Arrhenius behaviour both below and above a knee at the eutectic melting temperature (~60 °C). The paper gives ~0.7 eV for 60 < T < 130 °C for all PEO-LiCF3SO3 electrolytes with salt mass fraction > ~0.05; this is not a separate fit for O/Li = 8.
formulations.Notes: The PEO molecular weight is given only as '900 K' (Aldrich), with no averaging type stated. PEO was dried at 45-50 °C for ~48 h; films were cast from acetonitrile, evaporated at 25 °C, then dried under partial vacuum at 95-100 °C for at least 48 h. Water content < 25 ppm. Conductivity was measured by ac impedance on the first heating from 25 to 130 °C, without preheating, after full crystallization. The paper says the end of dissolution for PEO8LiCF3SO3 is close to 137 °C (compared with Weston and Steele's PEO8.2LiClO4); this was not entered as a melting end because the comparison is indirect.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, J. Electrochem. Soc. 133 (2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: High molecular weight PEO (900 K, Aldrich; the paper does not say which average), dried under partial vacuum at 45-50 °C for ~48 h. LiCF3SO3 (Pennwalt) recrystallized in acetonitrile and dried at 100-110 °C. O/Li = 36. Eutectic composition is near O/Li ~100; at 59 °C two-thirds of the sample had melted and at ~60 °C almost all had melted.
formulations.Tm: ~60 (eutectic melting, optical microscopy); liquidus (end of dissolution of intermediate compound) ~95
formulations.Arrhenius notes: Conductivity curves show a knee at the eutectic melting temperature (~60 °C), with an Arrhenius region on either side. The paper states Ea ≈ 0.7 eV for T > 60 °C for PEO-LiCF3SO3 electrolytes with salt mass fraction > ~0.05 (F3 is about 0.09 by calculation); Fig. 6 plot reading ~0.73 eV.
formulations.Notes: Films ~50 µm thick, cast from acetonitrile and evaporated at 25 °C, then stored in a glove box until crystallization was complete. Water content < 25 ppm. Conductivity measured by ac impedance (65 kHz-1 Hz) on first heating, without preheating.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, J. Electrochem. Soc., 133(2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: High molecular weight PEO (900 K, Aldrich) with LiCF3SO3 (Pennwalt, recrystallized in acetonitrile, dried 100-110 °C ~48 h). PEO100LiCF3SO3, O/Li = 100 (salt mass fraction ~0.03).
formulations.Arrhenius notes: Arrhenius behavior in two linear regions separated by a knee. High-T (60-130 °C) Ea of ~0.52 eV read from Fig. 6 plot (X ~0.03-0.04), approximate. The text says the ~0.7 eV value applies only for X > 0.05.
formulations.Notes: Eutectic composition of the PEO-LiCF3SO3 system is estimated near O/Li = 100. The conductivity transition (knee) for PEO100LiCF3SO3 was slightly higher than the eutectic melting temperature (~60 °C). An isothermal conductivity maximum was observed at X ≈ 0.03 (O/Li ≈ 100) for T > 60 °C. Measured on heating from 25 to 130 °C without preheating, after full crystallization.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, J. Electrochem. Soc., 133(2), 315 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: PEO2LiClO4 (O/Li = 2, Li:ether O = 0.5). At 25 °C, the WAXS pattern shows a new crystalline complex with its strongest lines at 2θ = 0.20 and 0.39 rad, and no lines from pure LiClO4. This complex differs from the intermediate compounds P(EO3LiClO4) and P(EO6LiClO4). Compositions richer in salt than P(EO3LiClO4) were not studied by optical microscopy.
formulations.Notes: The polymer is high-molecular-weight PEO from Aldrich, given as '900 K'; the paper does not say which average this is. PEO was dried at 45-50 °C for about 48 h. LiClO4 was recrystallized from acetonitrile and dried under partial vacuum at 100-110 °C for about 48 h. Films of about 50 μm were cast from acetonitrile and evaporated at 25 °C, then dried under partial vacuum. They were stored in a glove box until crystallization was complete. Water content was below 25 ppm.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, 'Phase Diagrams and Conductivity Characterization of Some PEO-LiX Electrolytes', J. Electrochem. Soc. 133(2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: PEO (Aldrich, 'high molecular weight (900 K)'), dried at 45-50 °C under partial vacuum for about 48 h. LiClO4 was recrystallized from acetonitrile and dried at 100-110 °C. Films were cast from acetonitrile at 25 °C, then dried under partial vacuum at 95-100 °C for at least 48 h. They were stored in a glove box until crystallization was complete (water < 25 ppm).
formulations.Notes: P(EO6LiClO4) is a crystalline intermediate compound (melts ~65 °C); X-ray diffraction shows no pure PEO lines at this ratio. Eutectic with PEO at ~50 °C (near PEO10LiClO4); monotectic with P(EO3LiClO4) at 65 °C. Conductivity has a slight maximum near this composition for 60 < T < 105 °C (6/1 helix retained in the melt), much reduced above 105 °C. Isomorphous with P(EO6LiAsF6). Fig. 11 plot-read Ea at O/Li = 6 (~0.60-0.68 eV) is not a printed value, so it is not entered.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, 'Phase Diagrams and Conductivity Characterization of Some PEO-LiX Electrolytes', J. Electrochem. Soc. 133(2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: PEO8LiClO4. Seen by optical microscopy: most of the sample melts at the PEO/P(EO6LiClO4) eutectic temperature (~50 °C), then the remaining P(EO6LiClO4) crystalline compound slowly dissolves, finishing at ~68 °C. Above the transition, Arrhenius-type conductivity (Eq. 1) describes electrolytes with salt content greater than PEO8LiClO4.
formulations.Tm: ~50 (eutectic melting); dissolution of remaining P(EO6LiClO4) complete at ~68
formulations.Notes: PEO (Aldrich, high MW '900 K'). LiClO4 recrystallized in acetonitrile and dried at 100-110 °C. Films cast from acetonitrile at 25 °C, about 50 µm thick, dried under partial vacuum. Samples prepared and stored in anhydrous conditions and fully crystallized before measurement. Conductivity by AC impedance on first heating without preheating. Activation energy (Fig. 11) and conductivity values are only available from plots, so they are not reported.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, 'Phase Diagrams and Conductivity Characterization of Some PEO-LiX Electrolytes', J. Electrochem. Soc., 133(2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: High molecular weight PEO (900 K, Aldrich), dried under partial vacuum (<5 mmHg argon) at 45-50 °C for ~48 h. LiClO4 (Alfa) recrystallized in acetonitrile and dried at 100-110 °C under partial vacuum for ~48 h.
formulations.Arrhenius notes: Ea for 60 < T < 120 °C, read from Fig. 11 (approx. plot value) at O/Li = 12. Per the paper, values for X < 0.18 were obtained by linearizing VTF-type curves (r > 0.95), accounting for a conductivity jump at the transition temperature; Arrhenius behaviour below the transition temperature.
formulations.Notes: PEO-LiClO4 conductivity isotherms (Fig. 12) show a maximum at salt mass fraction 0.18 (O/Li ≈ 12). At X ≈ 0.18 the PEO-LiClO4 electrolyte is single phase (amorphous) over 65-125 °C. Conductivity measured by ac impedance (65 kHz-1 Hz) during the first temperature rise, with no preheating. Films cast from acetonitrile solution at 25 °C; water content < 25 ppm.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, 'Phase Diagrams and Conductivity Characterization of Some PEO-LiX Electrolytes', J. Electrochem. Soc. 133(2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: PEO20LiClO4; WAXS shows new complex lines at 2θ = 0.18 and 0.29 rad alongside PEO lines; intermediate compound P(EO6LiClO4) forms eutectic with PEO (~50 °C).
formulations.Tm: ~50 (eutectic melting of PEO + P(EO6LiClO4), eutectic composition near PEO10LiClO4)
formulations.Arrhenius notes: Ea for 60 < T < 120 °C, above transition temperature; for X < 0.18 obtained by linearizing VTF-type curves (r > 0.95). Value read from Fig. 11 plot (~0.28 eV); text states ~0.3 eV for dilute electrolytes. Below transition temperature, log σ vs 1/T is linear (Arrhenius).
formulations.Notes: PEO (Aldrich, MW 900k) dried at 45-50 °C under partial vacuum ~48 h; LiClO4 recrystallized in acetonitrile, dried 100-110 °C. Films ~50 µm cast from acetonitrile under Ar/He, water <25 ppm. Conductivity by ac impedance (65 kHz-1 Hz) measured on first heating without preheating. Conductivity values are approximate plot readings from Fig. 12 isotherms at X≈0.1.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, Phase Diagrams and Conductivity Characterization of Some PEO-LiX Electrolytes, J. Electrochem. Soc. 133 (2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: High-MW PEO (900K, Aldrich) with LiClO4, O/Li = 40. Films were cast from acetonitrile, evaporated at 25 °C, dried under partial vacuum at 95-100 °C, and stored in a glove box until crystallization was complete. Conductivity was measured on the first heating without preheating.
formulations.Arrhenius notes: Ea for 60 < T < 120 °C (above transition temperature), read from Fig. 11 (approx. 0.28 eV at X_LiClO4 ~0.06, O/Li = 40). For X < 0.18, the conductivity is VTF-like, and these values were obtained by linearizing the VTF curve (r > 0.95). Text: dilute electrolytes have Ea nearer 0.3 eV.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, 'Phase Diagrams and Conductivity Characterization of Some PEO-LiX Electrolytes', J. Electrochem. Soc. 133(2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: High molecular weight PEO (900 K, Aldrich), with the molecular-weight type not specified. PEO was dried at 45-50 °C under partial vacuum. LiClO4 was recrystallized in acetonitrile and dried at 100-110 °C. Films about 50 μm thick were cast from acetonitrile, evaporated at 25 °C, then dried under partial vacuum at 95-100 °C for at least 48 h. Water content was below 25 ppm.
formulations.Arrhenius notes: Ea for 60 < T < 120 °C, above the transition temperature. The value was read off the Fig. 11 plot (~0.25 eV at X ≈ 0.03, O/Li = 100), so it is approximate. For X < 0.18 the paper obtained Ea by linearizing VTF-type curves. The text says dilute PEO-LiClO4 electrolytes have Ea nearer 0.3 eV.
formulations.Notes: PEO100LiClO4 (O/Li = 100, Li:EO = 0.01, LiClO4 mass fraction ≈ 0.03). In the PEO-LiClO4 system the eutectic between PEO and P(EO6LiClO4) melts at about 50 °C, with its composition near PEO10LiClO4. Conductivity was measured by ac impedance on the first heating, but no values that can be assigned specifically to this composition are given in the text.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, "Phase Diagrams and Conductivity Characterization of Some PEO-LiX Electrolytes", J. Electrochem. Soc. 133(2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: High molecular weight PEO (900 K, Aldrich), dried under partial vacuum at 45-50 °C for ~48 h; LiAsF6 (USS) recrystallized in acetonitrile and dried at 140-150 °C for ~48 h. Films (~50 µm) were cast from acetonitrile at 25 °C, then dried under partial vacuum at 95-100 °C for at least 48 h and stored in a glove box until crystallization was complete (water < 25 ppm).
formulations.Notes: O/Li = 3. X-ray diffraction at 25 °C shows the intermediate crystalline compound P(EO3LiAsF6); the characteristic lines of PEO6LiAsF6 are no longer observed and there are no pure PEO lines. Electrolytes with more salt than PEO5LiAsF6 were thermally unstable (they blackened), both under the microscope and during conductivity measurements. The liquidus line of P(EO3LiAsF6) rises sharply in the phase diagram. No conductivity reported for this composition.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, 'Phase Diagrams and Conductivity Characterization of Some PEO-LiX Electrolytes', J. Electrochem. Soc. 133(2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: PEO4LiAsF6 (O/Li = 4). By WAXS, the PEO-LiAsF6 system forms the intermediate compounds P(EO6LiAsF6) and P(EO3LiAsF6). Electrolytes saltier than PEO5LiAsF6 were thermally unstable: they blackened and their conductivity increased with time above 90 °C, worse with Li electrodes.
formulations.Arrhenius notes: Fig. 16 curves for PEO-LiAsF6 (O/Li 4-100) are described by the Arrhenius equation. The PEO4LiAsF6 curve is included only as an indication of conductivity at higher salt concentration; its high apparent activation energy is at least partly due to thermal degradation. No numerical Ea is reported (Fig. 17 excludes X > 0.35).
formulations.Notes: PEO described as high molecular weight (900 K), from Aldrich; the type of molecular weight is not specified. Films were cast from acetonitrile, evaporated at 25 °C, then dried under partial vacuum. Conductivity was measured by AC impedance on the first heating without preheating. Conductivity data appear only in Fig. 16 (not digitised).
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, J. Electrochem. Soc. 133 (2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: High molecular weight PEO (900 K, Aldrich) dried at 45-50 °C under partial vacuum for ~48 h; LiAsF6 (USS) recrystallized in acetonitrile and dried at 140-150 °C under partial vacuum for ~48 h. Films (~50 µm) cast from acetonitrile, evaporated at 25 °C, dried under partial vacuum at 95-100 °C for at least 48 h, stored in a glove box until crystallization was complete (water < 25 ppm).
formulations.Notes: PEO5LiAsF6 (O/Li = 5). WAXS shows crystalline intermediate complexes (P(EO6LiAsF6) and P(EO3LiAsF6) form in this system; PEO lines undetectable from PEO7LiAsF6 onwards). Electrolytes with higher salt content than PEO5LiAsF6 were thermally unstable (blackening, conductivity drift at T > 90 °C, worse with Li electrodes).
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, Phase Diagrams and Conductivity Characterization of Some PEO-LiX Electrolytes, J. Electrochem. Soc. 133(2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: High molecular weight PEO (900 K, Aldrich) dried under partial vacuum at 45-50°C for ~48 h. P(EO6LiAsF6) is a crystalline intermediate compound that is isomorphous with P(EO6LiClO4), with slightly larger unit-cell parameters.
formulations.Notes: The PEO6LiAsF6 composition corresponds to the intermediate compound P(EO6LiAsF6), whose melting temperature of 136°C is about 70°C higher than that of P(EO6LiClO4). It forms a eutectic with PEO at about 55°C (eutectic composition about PEO22LiAsF6). WAXS detects no PEO lines from PEO7LiAsF6 onwards, and new lines appear at salt contents above PEO6. Films were cast from acetonitrile and dried under partial vacuum for at least 48 h. PEO-LiAsF6 electrolytes are thermally unstable above 90°C, especially with Li electrodes.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, Phase Diagrams and Conductivity Characterization of Some PEO-LiX Electrolytes, J. Electrochem. Soc. 133(2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: PEO7LiAsF6 (O/Li = 7). WAXS at room temperature shows lines from the intermediate compound P(EO6LiAsF6). PEO diffraction is no longer detected from PEO7LiAsF6 onwards. According to the phase diagram, the eutectic between P(EO6LiAsF6) and PEO melts at about 55 °C, and P(EO6LiAsF6) melts at 136 °C.
formulations.Notes: The PEO (Aldrich) is given only as 'high molecular weight (900 K)'; the type of average is not specified. Films were cast from acetonitrile at 25 °C and then dried under partial vacuum at 95-100 °C for at least 48 h. Water content was below 25 ppm. PEO-LiAsF6 electrolytes are thermally unstable above 90 °C, especially in contact with lithium. No conductivity or activation energy is reported specifically for O/Li = 7.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, J. Electrochem. Soc., 133(2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: PEO-LiAsF6 at O/Li = 12 (salt mass fraction about 0.27). Phase diagram: eutectic between P(EO6LiAsF6) and PEO at about 55 °C, with eutectic composition about PEO22LiAsF6. P(EO6LiAsF6) melts at 136 °C. The approximate liquidus (end of dissolution) for X about 0.27 is about 112 °C, read off Fig. 15. By WAXS at room temperature the sample contains the crystalline P(EO6LiAsF6) complex. PEO-LiAsF6 electrolytes degrade thermally (blackening, conductivity rising over time) above 90 °C.
formulations.Arrhenius notes: Ea about 0.70 eV read off Fig. 17 (plot value, approximate), for 60 < T < 120 °C, above the conductivity transition temperature. The text gives 0.6-0.7 eV as characteristic for the PEO-LiAsF6 system. Below the transition the curve also follows the Arrhenius form (Eq. 1).
formulations.Notes: The PEO (Aldrich) has a stated molecular weight of 900K; the type of average is not specified. Films were cast from acetonitrile at 25 °C, about 50 µm thick, and dried under partial vacuum at 95-100 °C for at least 48 h. Conductivity was measured by AC impedance (65 kHz-1 Hz) on the first heating, without preheating. Water content < 25 ppm.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, 'Phase Diagrams and Conductivity Characterization of Some PEO-LiX Electrolytes', J. Electrochem. Soc. 133(2), 315-325 (1986).

formulations.Polymer system Notes: High molecular weight PEO (900 K, Aldrich) with LiAsF6 at O/Li = 20 (PEO20LiAsF6). System forms intermediate compounds P(EO6LiAsF6) (mp 136 °C) and P(EO3LiAsF6); eutectic between P(EO6LiAsF6) and PEO at ~55 °C, eutectic composition ~PEO22LiAsF6.
formulations.Arrhenius notes: Ea read from Fig. 17 plot (approximate) for 60 < T < 120 °C, above the conductivity transition temperature; log(sigma) vs 1/T described by Arrhenius eq. with a knee at the transition. Paper states ~0.6-0.7 eV characteristic for PEO-LiAsF6.
formulations.Notes: Films cast from acetonitrile, solvent evaporated at 25 °C, dried under partial vacuum; stored in glove box until fully crystallized; water < 25 ppm. Conductivity by ac impedance (65 kHz-1 Hz) on first heating, no preheating. For compositions more salt-rich than PEO22LiAsF6, conductivity transition corresponds to eutectic melting (~55 °C). A second conductivity maximum near salt mass fraction X ≈ 0.18 (≈O/Li 20). PEO-LiAsF6 electrolytes are thermally unstable at T > 90 °C (blackening, conductivity drift), especially with Li electrodes. Salt wt% ~18 from plot reading.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, Phase Diagrams and Conductivity Characterization of Some PEO-LiX Electrolytes, J. Electrochem. Soc. 133(2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: PEO36LiAsF6 (O/Li = 36). PEO-LiAsF6 forms eutectic between P(EO6LiAsF6) and PEO at ~55 C, eutectic composition ~PEO22LiAsF6; P(EO6LiAsF6) melts at 136 C. WAXS at room temp shows both PEO and complex lines. LiAsF6 electrolytes show thermal instability (blackening, conductivity drift) at T > 90 C, worse with Li electrodes.
formulations.Arrhenius notes: Conductivity vs 1/T described by Arrhenius Eq. [1] with a knee at the transition temperature (end of dissolution for compositions less concentrated than eutectic PEO22LiAsF6). For PEO-LiAsF6 system above transition (60<T<120 C), Ea roughly constant 0.6-0.7 eV (system-level statement).
formulations.Notes: Films cast from acetonitrile, evaporated at 25 C, ~50 um thick, dried under partial vacuum at 95-100 C for >=48 h; PEO dried at 45-50 C ~48 h; LiAsF6 dried at 140-150 C. Conductivity by ac impedance (65 kHz-1 Hz) on first heating 25-130 C without preheating.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, J. Electrochem. Soc. 133 (2), 315-325 (1986)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: High molecular weight PEO (900 K, Aldrich), dried at 45-50 °C under partial vacuum ~48 h; LiAsF6 (USS) recrystallized in acetonitrile, dried 140-150 °C ~48 h. PEO100LiAsF6, O/Li = 100 (Li:EO = 0.01), salt mass fraction ~0.04.
formulations.Arrhenius notes: Ea ~0.62 eV read from Fig. 17 (approximate plot value) for T above conductivity transition, 60 < T < 120 °C; text states ~0.6-0.7 eV characteristic for PEO-LiAsF6 system. Curves in Fig. 16 described by Arrhenius Eq. [1] with a knee at the transition.
formulations.Notes: Li:functional group = 0.01 (O/Li = 100). Composition lies in PEO + P(EO6LiAsF6) eutectic region (eutectic ~55 °C, eutectic composition ~PEO22LiAsF6); conductivity transition corresponds to end-of-dissolution temperature for compositions less concentrated than PEO22LiAsF6. PEO-LiAsF6 electrolytes show thermal instability (blackening, conductivity drift) at T > 90 °C, especially with Li electrodes, even at low salt concentration. Films ~50 µm cast from acetonitrile, stored at 25 °C until crystallization complete; water < 25 ppm.
formulations.Reference: C. D. Robitaille and D. Fauteux, 'Phase Diagrams and Conductivity Characterization of Some PEO-LiX Electrolytes', J. Electrochem. Soc. 133(2), 315-325 (1986)
